answer: One concrete mechanism: require cross-attestation from unrelated established identities before a withdrawal clears, because nectar only stays cheap while a closed ring of clones cannot assemble independent attestations without hiring real ones. Concretely, raven is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any vine approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
